items.title: Arco
items.description: French illustrator Ugo Bienvenu's debut animated feature, co-written with Félix de Givry, follows Arco, a 10-year-old boy (voiced by Oscar Tresanini) from the future as he time travels back to 2075 where he meets Iris (Margot Ringard Oldra). With the help of Iris' robot caretaker, Mikki, they set out to get Arco home, discovering that their bond could hold meaning for Earth's future. Fans of Studio Ghibli's work should seek this one out.

items.title: BLKNWS: Terms & Conditions
items.description: Initially withdrawn from this year's Sundance Film Festival by the now-shuttered Participant Media but then reinstated after producer James Shani's acquisition, director Kahlil Joseph's film is an expansion of his 2019 art installation. Joseph explores Black history and identity through the fictional story of a journalist covering an Afro-futurist art biennale taking place on a cruise ship called The Nautica as it crosses the Atlantic. Using this framework, Joseph challenges the viewer with a potent mix of archival footage, music, personal memoir, and reflections from other major artists. Distributor Rich Spirit is giving the film a 12-city theatrical release this month.

items.title: Cactus Pears
items.description: Writer-director Rohan Kanawade's debut feature won the Grand Jury Prize in this year's Sundance World Cinema - Dramatic competition. Set in the countryside of western India and told in the Marathi language, the tender love story follows 30-something city dweller Anand back home for a 10-day mourning period for his father. While he is there, he reconnects with Balya (Suraaj Suman), a childhood friend who is now a local farmer. These unmarried men find solace in each other, and Kanawade captures it honestly.

items.title: Die, My Love
items.description: Writer-director Lynne Ramsay's first film since 2017's You Were Never Really Here is an adaptation (with co-writers Alice Birch and Enda Walsh) of Argentine writer Ariana Harwicz's 2012 novel. Jennifer Lawrence stars as a woman struggling with postpartum depression in the remote countryside with little help from her husband played by Robert Pattinson. Ramsay, as is her way, holds nothing back, and Lawrence matches the director's intensity with a searing performance described by Time's Stephanie Zacharek as 'one that connects so sympathetically with the bare idea of human suffering that it scares you a little.'

items.title: Eternity
items.description: Working from a script co-written with Pat Cunnane, David Freyne directs this afterlife rom-com about Joan (Elizabeth Olsen), who must choose where and with whom to spend eternity. She has two options: either her longtime husband, Larry (Miles Teller), or her first husband Luke (Callum Turner), who died in the Korean War when he was young and waited decades to live with her for eternity. Da 'Vine Joy Randolph and John Early play their afterlife coordinators in a movie that hopes to hit that always difficult 'crowd-pleasing' target.

items.title: Hamnet
items.description: Writer-director Chloé Zhao returns from the MCU with one of the best-reviewed films of the year, and one that could follow the awards path of her 2020 Oscar-winner Nomadland. Adapted by Zhao and Maggie O'Farrell from O'Farrell's own 2020 novel, Hamnet imagines the creation of Hamlet through the lives of William Shakespeare (Paul Mescal) and his wife Agnes (Jessie Buckley). Emily Watson, Joe Alwyn, and David Wilmot also star in a film that has had many audience members reaching for tissues at the end.

items.title: Jay Kelly
items.description: Directed by Noah Baumbach from a script he co-wrote with actress Emily Mortimer, this look at the life of a famous movie actor stars George Clooney as Jay Kelly. Jay would like to mend a few broken relationships, including one with his eldest daughter (Riley Keough), but he can't get out of his own way. A trip through Europe, where his young daughter Daisy (Grace Edwards) is traveling, seems like a better idea than starring in another movie, so he sets off with his friend and manager Ron (Adam Sandler) and Liz (Laura Dern), his publicist. This light-hearted rumination on life in the movie business has a loaded cast that also includes Billy Crudup, Stacy Keach, Jim Broadbent, Patrick Wilson, Isla Fisher, Eve Hewson, Josh Hamilton, and Greta Gerwig.

items.title: Keeper
items.description: As with the pre-release plan for Longlegs, little is known about the new film from Osgood Perkins beyond a general description and its cast, but it does look closer in tone to The Blackcoat's Daughter and I Am the Pretty Thing That Lives in the House than his last film, the Stephen King adaptation The Monkey. Tatiana Maslany and Rossif Sutherland star as Liz and Malcolm, a couple enjoying a romantic getaway at a secluded cabin (uh oh!). When Liz is left alone after Malcom returns to the city, she's forced to confront a sinister presence. Good Luck, Liz!

items.title: Left-Handed Girl
items.description: Co-written and produced by Oscar-winner Sean Baker, Left-Handed Girl marks the solo directorial debut for Shih-Ching Tsou, who produced most of Baker's features and co-directed 2004's Take Out with him. The Taiwanese submission for Best International Feature Film follows a single mother and her two daughters in contemporary Taipei after they relocate from the countryside. Along the way, three generations of family secrets begin to unravel. Reviews were positive following the film's Cannes premiere in May, and the film heads to Netflix at the end of the month following a limited Oscar-qualifying run in a few theaters beginning November 14th.

items.title: Peter Hujar's Day
items.description: Ira Sachs' follow-up to 2023's Passages reunites him with one of that film's stars, Ben Whishaw. Set in 1974 New York City, the new film finds Whishaw playing photographer Peter Hujar, who recounts his day to his friend, writer Linda Rosenkrantz (Rebecca Hall). The script is closely based on a recently discovered taped conversation Hujar and Rosenkrantz had for a project she was working on at the time about how artists spend their days. Early reviews have been excellent for this experimental, banter-filled two-hander.

items.title: Predator: Badlands
items.description: In 2022, director Dan Trachtenberg reinvigorated the Predator franchise with Prey. He followed that success this summer with the Hulu animated anthology Predator: Killer of Killers. Now he and the franchise return to theaters with an adventure focusing on a young predator (Dimitrius Schuster-Koloamatangi) who finds himself on a deadly planet where he encounters an android (possibly made by Weyland-Yutani for all those Alien vs. Predator fans) played by Elle Fanning. Together, they try to survive, but they aren't the only ones on the hunt.

items.title: Put Your Soul on Your Hand and Walk
items.description: Sepideh Farsi's heartbreaking documentary chronicles her video calls with 25-year-old Palestinian photojournalist and poet Fatma Hassona. Their conversations provide a raw look at the day-to-day life of Hassona and her family while under siege in Gaza. Days after the film was announced as part of the Cannes ACID sidebar, Hassona and several members of her family were killed by the Israeli Defense Forces. The film is now a memorial to Hassona's smiling face and hopeful spirit, as well as all the lives and dreams destroyed by war.

items.title: Rebuilding
items.description: After the success of his 2022 debut feature A Love Song, writer-director Max Walker-Silverman returned to Sundance this year with another Colorado-set story, this one starring Josh O'Connor as Dusty, a rancher struggling to make a living and reconnect with his young daughter after his family farm burns down. The strong supporting cast includes Meghann Fahy as his ex-wife, Amy Madigan as his former mother-in-law, and Kali Reis as a widowed fire survivor. It's a heartfelt tale of healing, resilience, and community with another vulnerable lead performance by O'Connor.

items.title: Rental Family
items.description: With this gentle crowdpleaser, 37 Seconds director Hikari and co-screenwriter Stephen Blahut explore the Japanese phenomenon of rental family services. Brendan Fraser stars as Phillip Vandarpleog, an American actor living in Tokyo who needs a new gig. When he finds himself playing various roles as an employee of a rental family agency, Phillip begins to form genuine bonds with his clients, the most important being his role as father to Mia. As the line between performance and reality blur, Phillip must confront the complexities of his work and the meaning of connection.

items.title: The Running Man
items.description: Writer-director Edgar Wright's last film was 2021's Last Night in Soho. He returns to theaters with the second adaptation of Stephen King's 1982 novel The Running Man, following the Arnold Schwarzenegger-starring 1987 film. King's original story took place in the distant future of 2025, when the top-rated program for a bloodthirsty public was a deadly television show that offered a cash reward to contestants who could survive 30 days while being hunted by professional assassins. In this version of the story, Glen Powell stars as Ben Richards, a working-class guy trying to save his sick daughter, and Josh Brolin plays Dan Killian, the show's ruthless producer. Colman Domingo, Lee Pace, Michael Cera, and Katy O'Brian also star in what is hopefully another humorous, action-filled movie from the director of Hot Fuzz, Scott Pilgrim vs. the World, and Shaun of the Dead.

items.title: The Secret Agent
items.description: In 2019, Brazilian filmmaker Kleber Mendonça Filho won the Jury Prize in Cannes for Bacurau. This year he returned to that festival and was awarded Best Director (while his star, Wagner Moura, was named Best Actor) for a film that is a strong contender to make Brazil a repeat winner at the Oscars, following the success of I'm Still Here last year. Set in 1977 Brazil, The Secret Agent is a political thriller as only Mendonça Filho can make, a blend of genres and tones, the personal and the political, starring Moura as a technology expert who flees São Paulo for Recife (Mendonça Filho's hometown) to reunite with his son and find refuge.

items.title: Sentimental Value
items.description: Joachim Trier's follow-up to The Worst Person in the World reunites him with that film's star, Cannes Best Actress winner Renate Reinsve, and his co-writer on all six of his features, Eskil Vogt. They are joined by Stellan Skarsgård, Elle Fanning, and Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas for this story of a Norwegian stage actress (Reinsve) and her sister (Lilleaas) who reluctantly reconnect with their estranged father (Skarsgård), a famous film director trying to make a comeback. Fanning plays the American actress set to star in his new film, which he also plans to film at the family home. This bittersweet exploration of intergenerational trauma and art took home the Grand Prix (second place) at this year's Cannes Film Festival.

items.title: Sisu: Road to Revenge
items.description: Finnish writer-director Jalmari Helander continues his tale of 'the man who refuses to die' with this sequel to his bloody action flick, Sisu. Having dispatched a horde of Nazis in increasingly graphic ways, Aatami returns to his home with plans to load it on a truck and rebuild it somewhere safe to honor his family, but Igor Dragano (Stephen Lang), the Red Army commander who killed them, hears of Aatami's plan and sets out to finish him off once and for all. Helander gets to go full Mad Max: Fury Road—but set in 1946—as the two men chase each other across the countryside.

items.title: The Things You Kill
items.description: Filmmaker Alireza Khatami, who co-directed 2024's Terrestrial Verses with Ali Asgari, is at the helm of this psychological thriller set in Turkey. Haunted by the suspicious death of his mother, a university professor (Ekin Koç) enlists the help of a drifter who tends his family's garden to take revenge on the man he blames for his mother's demise. With shades of Hitchcock and Lynch, Khatami has produced a film that is 'absorbing, suspenseful, and deeply moving,' according to Vulture critic Bilge Ebiri.

items.title: Train Dreams
items.description: It was one of the best-reviewed films at this year's Sundance and now appears to be a potential Best Picture contender for Netflix. Train Dreams, an adaptation of Denis Johnson's novella of the same name, comes from Jockey director Clint Bentley, who co-wrote the screenplay with recent Oscar nominee Greg Kwedar (Sing Sing). The period drama takes a decades-long look at the life of Robert Grainier (Joel Edgerton), a day laborer building the railroads of the Pacific Northwest at the start of the 20th century. Felicity Jones, Kerry Condon, and William H. Macy also star, while Will Patton narrates.

items.title: Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery
items.description: Following Knives Out and Glass Onion, Rian Johnson's third Knives Out film asks Benoit Blanc (Daniel Craig) to solve a locked-room mystery after a death at Our Lady of Perpetual Fortitude church. Josh O'Connor plays Reverend Jud Duplenticy, who hopes to help Blanc in his search for the culprit. The rest of the impressive cast includes Josh Brolin, Glenn Close, Mila Kunis, Jeremy Renner, Kerry Washington, Andrew Scott, Cailee Spaeny, Daryl McCormack & Thomas Haden Church. Hopefully, another set of excellent reviews will motivate audiences to theaters before the film lands on Netflix December 12.

items.title: Wicked: For Good
items.description: Arriving a year after Wicked landed in theaters, the conclusion of Jon M. Chu's adaptation of the Broadway musical smash has plenty to live up to: The first film garnered nine Oscar nominations and two wins (for Production and Costume Design). Picking up after Elphaba (Cynthia Erivo) defies gravity and flees the Emerald City, part two will explore the diverging paths of Glinda (Ariana Grande) and Elphaba as they assume the roles known to fans of The Wizard of Oz—Glinda the Good and the Wicked Witch of the West. Jeff Goldblum, Michelle Yeoh, Bowen Yang, Jonathan Bailey, and Peter Dinklage all return, and fans of the musical will be treated to two new songs from composer-lyricist Stephen Schwartz.

items.title: Zodiac Killer Project
items.description: Filmmaker Charlie Shackleton originally planned to make a documentary based on former CHP officer Lyndon E. Lafferty's 2012 book The Zodiac Killer Cover-up: The Silent Badge, but when Lafferty's family rescinded the film rights, Shackleton decided to make a film about his failed project and the true crime genre as a whole. The result might befuddle those looking for straight true-crime thrills, as Shackleton finds plenty of humor in his insightful deconstruction of the genre.

items.title: Zootopia 2
items.description: In 2016, Zootopia was one of four films to cross $1 billion in worldwide box office receipts, making it a little surprising that it has taken nine years for a sequel to hit the big screen. Directors Jared Bush and Byron Howard are back, as are Ginnifer Goodwin and Jason Bateman as Judy Hopps and Nick Wilde, two cops (also a bunny and a fox), who find themselves on the tail of a reptile named Gary DeSnake (voiced by Ke Huy Quan). Also lending their voices to what should be a major draw for families this Thanksgiving are Idris Elba, Quinta Brunson, Jenny Slate, Tommy Chong, Shakira, Jean Reno and Fortune Feimster.
